title: The Rope Guy
logline: Called for jury duty, Marshall hides that he's a lawyer so he can finally sit on a jury, tells the judge he's in rope, and cannot stop objecting. Ted, in the same jury pool, chases a better score from a judge who grades excuses like figure skating, while Robin and Barney run a book on how long Marshall lasts.

guests.name: Judge Harriet Vance
guests.role: A Manhattan civil judge who has heard every jury excuse in thirty years and scores each one out loud, like Olympic figure skating. Never surprised, never raises her voice.

guests.name: Walter Pulaski
guests.role: A retired mailman suing the Benedict Arnold's brunch chain after slipping on hollandaise. Represents himself in his old postal uniform and objects whenever he thinks it's his turn.

facts.marshall.job: lawyer at a big Manhattan firm
facts.marshall.pro_bono: Walter Pulaski's lawyer vs. Benedict Arnold's brunch chain; Brad defends
facts.marvin.jury_duty: St. Cloud jury, 1986 (Gus and the canoe); never told Marshall the verdict
facts.ted.jury_duty: always dodged it; seated once by Judge Vance, excused as Marshall's roommate
facts.barney.jury_duty: excused nine times by Judge Vance for answering 'Please.' Scored a 9.6
facts.robin.jury_duty: not a US citizen, can't serve; holds the money on the gang's bets

opens.note: Marshall's pro bono case for Walter Pulaski against Benedict Arnold's, with Brad defending; the verdict hasn't been decided

scenes.summary: In motion, mid voir dire. Marshall in the jury box claims to be a regular guy in rope, wearing his good suit. Brad, defending the brunch chain, recognizes him and covers for him. Walter, representing himself, makes his statement. Marshall objects to Brad's clogs remark and covers badly; the judge sustains it. Runner 1: a whispered Lawyered, and 'Bless you.'

beats.line: Juror number eleven. Occupation?
I'm a regular guy, Your Honor. Just a regular, everyday, normal guy.
That's not an occupation, Mr. Eriksen. That's a jingle.
I'm in rope.
Rope.
Mostly rope. Some twine. Twine is seasonal.
Marsh? Bro. You're wearing a three-hundred-dollar suit.
Rope has been very good to me.
Mr. Morris. Do you know this juror?
From brunch, Your Honor. Everybody knows everybody from brunch.
Mr. Pulaski, you're representing yourself. Anything for this juror?
I carried the mail thirty-one years. Rain, sleet, snow. Nobody ever said anything about hollandaise.
Your Honor, the jury should know Mr. Pulaski was wearing clogs.
Objection!
To clogs. As a regular guy. Those things are death traps.
Sustained, actually. Save the footwear for trial, Mr. Morris.
Lawyered.
Bless you.
Thank you, Your Honor.

scenes.summary: Barney opens the Eriksen Book; Robin holds the money because a Canadian can't serve on an American jury. The lines, including Lawyered out loud at three to one. Lily takes 'seated' at fifty to one and drags Marshall home to normal school.

beats.line: Ladies and gentlemen. The Eriksen Book is officially open.
You're gambling on my civic dream?
Marshall, I've bet on every big moment of your life. Your bar exam. Your wedding. Your first mechanical bull.
Lost a fortune on the bull.
I hold the money. I'm Canadian, so I can't serve on an American jury. I'm the only impartial person in this bar.
Current lines. Marshall gets struck before lunch: even money.
Marshall says Lawyered, out loud, in open court: three to one.
Over-under on the word precedent: four and a half.
I'm not getting struck. I'm a regular guy. The judge loved the rope.
Baby, you told a judge twine is seasonal.
Marshall actually gets seated on the jury: fifty to one. Barney wanted a thousand to one. I'm Canadian. I said fifty.
I'll take that. Twenty bucks.
At fifty to one? Lily, that's a thousand dollars.
I know math, Barney. I teach it to people who eat paste.
Lilypad. You believe in me.
I believe in me. Up. Tonight, you're going to normal school.
Is there a snack?

scenes.summary: Lily trains Marshall to be normal, holding his meatball sub hostage: one bite per lawyery word. Runner 2: Lawyered becomes Law-nice.

beats.line: Rule one. Every time you say something lawyery, I take a bite of your meatball sub.
Lily, that's cruel and unusual.
Bite.
A guy cuts in front of you at the deli. Go.
Hey, buddy. Not cool. Under the first-in-time doctrine—
Bite.
You win an argument. What do you say?
Lawy—
Sandwich.
Nice! Law-nice. Law-nice is a nice word.

scenes.summary: Ted arrives from the jury pool. Future Ted claims jury duty is sacred; Penny and Luke catch him. Ted's architectural excuse scored a 3.1. Barney's one-word excuse got a 9.6. Robin opens a line on Ted.

beats.line: Now, I've always considered jury duty a sacred trust.
Dad. How many juries have you actually served on?
I have been summoned many times.
That's not what I asked.
I have been excused many times. For architectural reasons.
What's an architectural reason?
Your Honor, this courthouse bolts Ionic columns onto a parking garage. I cannot be impartial inside a lie.
And?
Three point one.
She scored you?
She scores every excuse. Like figure skating. A guy with a sick goldfish got a five.
Amateur. I've been summoned nine times. Same judge, same one word.
Occupation?
Please.
Nine point six. Excused.
One word? My excuse had footnotes!
New line. Ted cracks a nine tomorrow: twenty to one.
Twenty bucks. I'm bringing a diagram.

scenes.summary: One bite left. Lily asks why it matters; Marshall says 'a civic thing' and Lily knows it isn't the whole story. She eats the last bite. Objection, sustained.

beats.line: Final exam. Why does this matter so much to you?
It's a civic thing.
That's the least lawyery thing you've said all night. That's how I know it's not the whole story.
Can I please have the last bite? I've been very regular today.
Never say that in court.
Also, objection.
Sustained.

scenes.label: Day two
scenes.summary: Ted's beige-cornice excuse gets a 6.2 and is denied. Marshall arrives in Lily's idea of regular clothes; Brad asks about rope. Marshall objects on Walter's behalf, Walter adopts it, and runner 2 lands in court: Law-nice.

beats.line: Mr. Mosby. You asked to supplement yesterday's excuse.
Your Honor, Benedict Arnold's is in a 1911 bank. They painted its terra-cotta cornice beige. I am not impartial. I am furious.
Six point two.
Personal best!
Denied. Sit down.
Mr. Eriksen. Love the flannel. You look like the guy on a paper towel.
This is how we dress in rope.
Tell me about rope.
It's long.
If Mr. Pulaski walked right past a wet floor sign, you'd agree that's on him, right?
Objection. Counsel's asking a juror to prejudge the evidence.
What he said!
Sustained.
Lawy—
Sandwich.
Law-nice.
Marsh. Bro. You're objecting for the other side.
There's no other side, Brad. There's just a guy. In rope.

scenes.summary: Barney and Robin at the bar mid-morning, working the book off Lily's texts. Law-nice does not count.

beats.line: Lily says Ted got a six point two. And Marshall's said precedent five times. The over hits.
Did he say Lawyered?
He said Law-nice.
Does Law-nice count?
The book says out loud and in full. Law-nice is a pastry.
God, I love it when you run the book. Say 'the over hits' again.
No.

scenes.summary: The judge puts Marshall under oath. He admits he's a lawyer and tells her why: Marvin's jury in St. Cloud, Gus and the canoe, four days of listening. He wanted to know if he's still one of the twelve. She excuses him. A quiet ending.

beats.line: Mr. Eriksen. In two days you've objected four times, cited two cases, and called my bailiff counselor.
You're under oath. Occupation.
I'm a lawyer, Your Honor.
I knew it. Nobody's in rope.
I've watched people fake comas to get off a jury. Why would a man lie to get on one?
When I was nine, my dad got called for jury duty. Back home in St. Cloud.
Marshall was nine. He was also already six foot four.
Son, a fella named Gus borrowed a canoe, and the whole town decided he stole it.
Took twelve of us four whole days just to listen to him.
I don't think anybody ever listened to Gus for four days. In his whole life.
Did he steal it, Dad?
Can't tell you, son. I took an oath.
Twelve regular people. Nobody ever asked them anything. And for four days, it was all up to them.
So I went to law school. Turns out that's the one thing that keeps you off a jury.
Now I've got a big firm and nice suits. I guess I wanted to know if I'm still one of the twelve.
Thirty years, I've scored every excuse to get off a jury. Nobody ever gave me a reason to get on one.
You're excused.

scenes.summary: Robin reads the news: Marshall's struck before lunch, Barney wins. Then the rest of Lily's text. Barney is allergic to sincerity.

beats.line: He's out. Struck at eleven fifty-two.
Before lunch! Daddy's getting paid!
Lily says he told the judge about his dad. The bailiff cried.
Let's hold that payout for a while.
Barney. Are you crying?
No. I'm allergic to sincerity. It's flaring up.

scenes.summary: Ted, who brought a 9.8 excuse with a fold-out, has none. Zero. Seated, in Marshall's old chair. Walter asks for the rope guy as his lawyer. Marshall takes the counsel table. Neither rain nor sleet nor hollandaise.

beats.line: Mr. Mosby. I'm told you brought a diagram.
I did, Your Honor. It's a nine point eight. It has a fold-out.
I don't have an excuse, Your Honor.
Zero point zero. Seated.
Your Honor? Can I have the rope guy?
He's been excused, Mr. Pulaski.
Not for the jury. For me. He's been objecting for me for two days. He's better at it than I am.
Mr. Eriksen. Are you licensed to practice in New York?
Yes, Your Honor.
Are you in rope?
No, Your Honor. I have never been in rope.
Then take that table. We resume Monday.
Neither rain, nor sleet, nor snow.
Nor hollandaise.

scenes.summary: Robin settles the Eriksen Book. Lily and Ted lose; Ted doesn't care, he has a juror notebook with a ribbon. Lily and Marshall whisper about the conflict Ted hasn't noticed. One bet is still open, and the book is confidential.

beats.line: Settling the Eriksen Book. Marshall seated on the jury: no. Lily owes twenty.
Ted cracks a nine: Ted got a zero. Ted owes twenty.
Worth it. I'm going to be the greatest juror this city has ever seen.
I bought a juror notebook. It's leather. It has a ribbon.
You have to tell him.
I have to tell the judge.
Tell the judge what?
That you're gonna be great, buddy.
One bet's still open. Lawyered, out loud, in court. Three to one.
Nobody took that bet.
Somebody did.
Who?
The book is confidential, Barney.

scenes.label: Monday
scenes.summary: Marshall, back in his suit at the counsel table, discloses that juror four is his roommate. Ted, who now wants to serve, pleads. Excused, 4.1. Marshall says it out loud: Lawyered. Lily collects at three to one; she coached him all week to drive the odds up. Barney is moved.

beats.line: Counsel. Anything before I swear in the jury?
Your Honor, I have to disclose something about juror number four.
Marshall?
He's my roommate.
Your Honor, I barely know this man.
We've shared a bathroom since 1996. He labels my leftovers. In Latin.
Defense would've struck him anyway, Your Honor. He has feelings about our cornice.
Marshall, I finally want to be here!
Sorry, buddy. Duty of candor to the tribunal.
You told this tribunal you were in rope!
Mr. Mosby, you're excused.
What's my score?
Four point one. Deductions for barely.
Did you just lawyer me?
Lawyered.
Yes!
Out loud. In full. In court. Three to one, Lily.
You spent all week coaching him not to say it!
Exactly. Four days, bottled up. Barney, it had to come out somewhere.
Lily Aldrin. That's the most beautiful thing I've ever heard.
